review_comments.body: **Pass-through restores rejected fields** If body pass-through is enabled on a Moonshot Chat Completions channel, the gateway replaces the filtered body with the client's original JSON. That restores the four sampling fields, so Moonshot can still reject a `kimi-k2.6` request with `temperature: 0.2`. Apply the same filter to the replayed body and leave unrelated fields intact. **Knowledge Base Used:** - [Provider protocol transformers](https://app.greptile.com/-/switch-tenant?tenant=looplj&next=%2Fcustom-context%2Fknowledge-base%2Flooplj%2Faxonhub%2F-%2Fdocs%2Fprovider-protocol-transformers.md) - [LLM execution pipelines](https://app.greptile.com/-/switch-tenant?tenant=looplj&next=%2Fcustom-context%2Fknowledge-base%2Flooplj%2Faxonhub%2F-%2Fdocs%2Fllm-execution-pipelines.md) Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time!

**Tests miss changed sampling values** For unaffected models, the test checks that each key exists, so it would still pass if the value changed or became `null`. Compare the values in the JSON with the ones in the request. ```suggestion if tt.keep { want := map[string]float64{ "temperature": 0.2, "top_p": 0.9, "presence_penalty": 0.1, "frequency_penalty": 0.1, } assert.Equal(t, want[k], body[k], "sampling parameter %s", k) ```
